# Summary

Reflecting on my MSc journey, bringing together my coursework, technical skill development, and the execution of my dissertation on clinical data integration, I can clearly see my transformation from a student into a capable researcher\[cite: 24\]. \*In hindsight\*, the most crucial advice I would give myself at the start of the programme would be to embrace the steep technical learning curve early on and to initiate conversations regarding PhD and career pathways from day one\[cite: 24\]. Regarding \*missing skills\*, I quickly realized that while I grasped the theoretical aspects of health data, I initially lacked the advanced computational proficiencies—such as managing High-Performance Clusters (HPC), optimizing Python environments, and utilizing robust version control like Git—that are essential for executing complex, large-scale AI research\[cite: 24\]. Looking toward \*future growth\*, my immediate next steps involve securing post-MSc Research Assistant experience to become a more competitive candidate for PhD funding, while simultaneously continuing to hone my applied healthcare data science skills to ensure I am highly prepared for both academic research and professional industry roles.
